notes.text: But he looking steadfastly up to heaven, saw the glory of God — Doubtless he saw such a glorious representation, God miraculously operating on his imagination, as on Ezekiel's, when he sat in his house at Babylon, and saw Jerusalem, and seemed to himself transported thither, chap. viii, 1-4. And probably other martyrs, when called to suffer the last extremity, have had extraordinary assistance of some similar kind.
I see the Son of man standing — As if it were just ready to receive him. Otherwise he is said to sit at the right hand of God.
They rushed upon him — Before any sentence passed.

The witnesses laid down their clothes at the feet of a young man, whose name was Saul — O Saul, couldst thou have believed, if one had told thee, that thou thyself shouldst be stoned in the same cause? and shouldst triumph in committing thy soul likewise to that Jesus whom thou art now blaspheming? His dying prayer reached thee, as well as many others. And the martyr Stephen, and Saul the persecutor, (afterward his brother both in faith and martyrdom,) are now joined in everlasting friendship, and dwell together in the happy company of those who have made their robes white in the blood of the Lamb.

And they stoned Stephen, invoking and saying, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit — This is the literal translation of the words, the name of God not being in the original. Nevertheless such a solemn prayer to Christ, in which a departing soul is thus committed into his hands, is such an act of worship, as no good man could have paid to a mere creature; Stephen here worshipping Christ in the very same manner in which Christ worshipped the Father on the cross.

glossa.text:
*Standing.* Immovably, because he is not *ite rum* to fall, or the bearing is signified of one helping, and judging wrongs, and fighting for his servant.

*I see the heavens. ((RAB.))* About to depart from the earth, he saw the heavens opened, that he who despised the earthly life for Christ might merit the inheritance of heaven, and therefore in his very suffering he sees the reward.

*The Son of man.* Although Christ is the Son of God, yet he chose rather to call him the Son of man, that the unbelief of the Jews might be confounded, who crucified him as a mere man, whom they would not believe to be God.
*And casting him out. ((RAB.))* In this they gloried that they fulfilled the law. For Moses said of the blasphemer: *Bring him forth without the camp, and let the people stone him ((Lev. XXIV))*.

*Lord Jesus, receive my spirit,* into the heaven which I see opened. Christ said to the Father: *Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit.* Stephen, as a servant to the Lord, *Lord,* etc.

*Because they know not. ((RAB.))* Many of them, in killing Stephen, thought that they fulfilled the law, because they believed him a blasphemer. This also Christ had foretold: *There shall come,* he says, *an hour, that everyone who killeth you may think that he rendereth a service to God ((Joan. XVI))*.

*He fell asleep.* Beautifully is it said, *He fell asleep,* and not, *He is dead,* because he offered the sacrifice of love, and fell asleep in the hope of the resurrection. The saints do not die, because they are changed for the better, and the temporal life is turned into the eternal.

*And Saul,* etc. He did not indeed stone him, but consented to them that stoned. Whence he would have perished, unless the grace of God and penance had come to his aid; because they who do and they who consent are worthy of death.

notes.text: Ashamed — Of my confidence in thy promise. Deliver me - According to thy faithfulness and goodness.

My spirit — My soul or life; to preserve it from the malice of mine enemies. For - Thou hast delivered me formerly, and therefore I commit myself to thee for the future. O Lord, &c. - Who hast shewed thyself so, in making good thy promise.

glossa.text: *In thee, O Lord, have I hoped,* etc. ((ID.)) There is an eternal confusion, from which he asks to be delivered: and there is a temporal one, for an hour, namely the kind that profits.

*Make haste.* ((ID.)) In the things to be done, in the souls to be loosed and the like, that thou mayest rescue me on the third day and not defer it to the common resurrection; and that this may be, be thou to me a protector as great as it befits God to be. *Be thou to me.* He said: Give justice, etc., *as far as* he affirms the deliverance.

*Thou wilt bring out.* ((CASS.)) From death to the things above, so that the counsels of the Jews may be in vain. *Out of the snare which they have hidden.* ((AUG.)) The devil tempts by two gates, etc., *as far as* whence: *Thou wilt bring me out of the snare.*

*Into thy hands.* ((CASS.)) Note that he speaks here who uttered these same words in the passion. ((AUG.)) *Into thy hands.* From these words which he said on the cross, he gives notice that he has spoken in this psalm.

notes.text: Desire — Always, as earnestly as new born babes do, chap. i, 3. The milk of the word - That word of God which nourishes the soul as milk does the body, and which is sincere, pure from all guile, so that none are deceived who cleave to it. That you may grow thereby - In faith, love, holiness, unto the full stature of Christ.
Since ye have tasted — Sweetly and experimentally known.

To whom coming — By faith. As unto a living stone - Living from eternity; alive from the dead. There is a wonderful beauty and energy in these expressions, which describe Christ as a spiritual foundation, solid, firm, durable; and believers as a building erected upon it, in preference to that temple which the Jews accounted their highest glory. And St. Peter speaking of him thus, shows he did not judge himself, but Christ, to be the rock on which the church was built. Rejected indeed by men - Even at this day, not only by Jews, Turks, heathens, infidels; but by all Christians, so called, who live in sin, or who hope to be saved by their own works. But chosen of God - From all eternity, to be the foundation of his church. And precious - In himself, in the sight of God, and in the eyes of all believers.

Ye — Believers. As living stones - Alive to God through him. Are built up - In union with each other. A spiritual house - Being spiritual yourselves, and an habitation of God through the Spirit. An holy priesthood - Consecrated to God, and "holy as he is holy." To offer up - Your souls and bodies, with all your thoughts, words, and actions, as spiritual sacrifices to God.
He that believeth shall not be confounded — In time or in eternity. Isaiah xxviii, 16.

To them who believe, he is become the head of the corner — The chief corner stone, on which the whole building rests. Unbelievers too will at length find him such to their sorrow, Matt. xxi, 44. Psalm cxviii, 22.
Who stumble, whereunto also they were appointed — They who believe not, stumble, and fall, and perish forever; God having appointed from all eternity, "he that believeth not shall be damned."

But ye — Who believe in Christ Are - In a higher sense than ever the Jews were. A chosen or elect race, a royal priesthood - "Kings and priests unto God," Rev. i, 6. As princes, ye have power with God, and victory over sin, the world, and the devil: as priests, ye are consecrated to God, for offering spiritual sacrifices. Ye Christians are as one holy nation, under Christ your King. A purchased people - Who are his peculiar property. That ye may show forth - By your whole behaviour, to all mankind. The virtues - The excellent glory, the mercy, wisdom, and power of him, Christ, who hath called you out of the darkness of ignorance, error, sin, and misery.
Who in time past were not a people — Much less the people of God; but scattered individuals of many nations. The former part of the verse particularly respects the gentiles; the latter, the Jews.

glossa.text:
*As newborn babes. ((BEDA.))* Because you have been so born again, and made eternal sons, be such through the pursuit of a good conversation as newly born infants are through the nature of their age.

*Reasonable.* Be infants through malice put away, yet reasonable through wisdom: and let no reasoning draw you to the craftinesses of the world, but be without guile; whence: *Be ye wise as serpents ((Matth. X))*, etc.

*Desire milk. ((BEDA.))* He touches upon those who come fastidious to the hearing of the sacred lessons, ignorant of that thirst and hunger of which the Lord says: *Blessed are they that hunger and thirst after justice ((Matth. V))*. And therefore they come the more slowly to the perfect increases of salvation, whereby they might be able to be refreshed with the solid food of the word, that is, to know the divine secrets, or to do greater goods. *That you may grow thereby.* That also by learning well you may come, through the sacred things of the Lord's incarnation, to the contemplation of the divine majesty.

*If so be you have tasted. ((ID.))* In this manner, the malice of the heart being purged, desire the life-giving nourishment of Christ, if you have a savour of how great the divine sweetness is. For he who tastes nothing of his sweetness, it is no wonder if he does not avoid to defile this man with earthly desires.

*As stones, men.* *viri*; read *vivi*, "living" Through unbelief indeed hard and insensible, but through discernment instructed, they are made alive and are fit to be joined together by charity in the building of God.

*Be ye built up.* Unto the offering of good works, alms, prayers, and your own selves. *Through Jesus Christ.* This is referred to all, you are built up, you are priests, you offer, and all this, through Jesus Christ, by whose grace you have all things.
*Wherefore* it must be established that the Lord, by reason of his firmness, is rightly called a stone, etc.

*To you therefore that believe there is honour to them that believe not,* etc., *whom the builders rejected.* So rejected by these as by those, and that stone here, that is to them that believe, *is made the head of the corner,* and to the unbelieving is made *a stone of stumbling and a rock of scandal.*

*And a stone of stumbling.* Whereas Christ is a stone in which the good are upheld and rest secure, to the unbelieving he shall be a cause of stumbling in the present, to them that believe not in him, and therefore they are falling from vice to vice. In the time to come he is a rock of scandal, because against that stone, Christ, whom they trod upon as lowly, their steps shall be dashed, and they shall fall into the eternal fire which is prepared for the devil and his angels. *They stumble at the word.* He stumbles at the word who does so by this, that he has heard the word; he stumbles in mind, while he does not believe what he has heard, whose foolishness he aggravates. *Nor do they believe in that wherein they are set:* by nature men were made unto this, that they should believe God and obey his will.

*But you are a chosen generation.* This testimony of praise, once given to the ancient people through Moses, the Apostle gives to the Gentiles who believe in Christ: who, as a corner stone, gathered the nations into that salvation which Israel had had in itself. *A kingly priesthood.* United to the body of the high priest, who were bound to hope for a kingdom, and to offer to God the victims of an unspotted conversation. *Of acquisition,* in the blood of his redemption, as the people of Israel was once redeemed out of Egypt by the blood of the lamb. Whence also in the following verse he mystically calls to mind the ancient history, and teaches that it was fulfilled specially in one people.

*That you may declare. ((BEDA.))* As they that were delivered out of Egypt sang a song of triumph to the Lord, so we, after the darkness was dissolved, after the remission received through Christ who leads us to the country of the supernal brightness, ought to repay to God thanks worthy of the heavenly benefits.

*Who in time past. ((ID.))* Hence it is proved that he writes this epistle to those who had come to the faith from among the Gentiles. These verses are taken from the prophecy of Osee, in which the calling of the Gentiles is treated of.

notes.text: Let not your heart be troubled — At my departure. Believe - This is the sum of all his discourse, which is urged till they did believe, Chap. xvi, 30. And then our Lord prays and departs.
In my Father's house are many mansions — Enough to receive both the holy angels, and your predecessors in the faith, and all that now believe, and a great multitude, which no man can number.
The way — Of faith, holiness, sufferings.
Thomas saith — Taking him in a gross sense.

To the question concerning the way, he answers, I am the way. To the question concerning knowledge, he answers, I am the truth. To the question whither, I am the life. The first is treated of in this verse; the second, ver. 7-17; the third, xiv, 18, &c.
Ye have known — Ye have begun to know him.
I am in the Father — The words that I speak, &c. - That is, I am one with the Father, in essence, in speaking, and in acting.
Believe me — On my own word, because I am God. The works - This respects not merely the miracles themselves, but his sovereign, Godlike way of performing them.

Greater works than these shall he do — So one apostle wrought miracles merely by his shadow, Acts v, 15; another by handkerchiefs carried from his body, Acts xix, 12; and all spake with various tongues. But the converting one sinner is a greater work than all these. Because I go to my Father - To send you the Holy Ghost.

glossa.text: *Let not your heart be troubled,* etc. ((AUG.)) But lest they should fear his death as a man's, and on that account be troubled, etc., *as far as* one glory of the moon, another glory of the stars.

*In the house,* etc. The house of God, the temple of God, the kingdom of God. The kingdom of heaven is just men, among whom there are many differences one from another. And these are the mansions of that same house.

((AUG.)) Just men are now the kingdom of God and the kingdom of heaven, etc., *as far as* that what you were in hope, you may be in reality.

*If otherwise,* etc. That is, if I had not predestined a mansion, which is unfitting as regards God, who predestined all good things before all times, then I should only now be preparing, that is, predestining, which again is unfitting, as regards God's predestining anything in the present.

((ID.)) He confirms that they are, because if they were not he would have said, I will go and will prepare, etc., *as far as* and this is the multitude of mansions.

*And if I shall go. ((ID.))* He went away by hiding, he came by appearing, but he remains by governing, that we may make progress by living well, and thus a place is prepared.

((ID.)) The faith which does not see believes, for if it saw, etc., *as far as* the desire of love is the preparation of a mansion.

*And whither I go.* This was said with respect to certain ones who knew both the Son and the Father. But Thomas, although he supposed himself not to know, is convicted by this, that he knew him, and knew both the way and the life, that is, the Son and the Father. Of these who knew, it is subjoined: From henceforth you shall know him, known through me, and you have seen him in the heart, while you have seen me like to him in all things.

*Thomas saith to him,* etc. He who does not lie said that they knew whither and by what way one goes; but Thomas says that they know neither, not knowing that they know; yet Christ convicts them of knowing, because if they knew him, and he is the way, they knew the way; and if they knew him, and he is the truth and the life, then they knew the truth and the life to which he goes: he therefore goes by himself as the way, to himself as truth and life, and to the Father, because he is one with the Father.

*If you had known me.* Because he had said that none comes to the Father except through himself, who is inseparably the same with the Father, lest they should ask who the Father is, he shows that from himself, once known, the Father is known, which certain ones had not yet known, whom he reproves, saying: *If you had known,* etc. *And you have seen him.* As it is said of two things wholly alike: If you have seen this one, you have seen that one; they had therefore seen the Son as most like [him], but they had to be admonished to understand the Father also to be such a one, and not unlike.

*How sayest thou.* And that, when he is wholly like. *How sayest thou,* etc. As if he should say: I see with what mind thou sayest it; thou dost not seek another like me, but thou thinkest [him] better. *Of myself.* Because I who speak am not of myself: he attributes to him what he does, of whom is he himself who does it.

*He that believeth in me.* I and the Father work without difference. And whosoever believes in me (lest this should be taken of the apostles alone), the works that I do through myself, he also shall do, that is, I do in him or through him, and even greater ones. *The works that I do.* Not however of himself, but of me. *The servant is not greater than his lord.* For he himself [does] many things without them, they without him nothing, save sin.

*Greater than these. ((AUG.))* Because if he himself [healed] by the hem of his garment, Peter healed by a shadow. Or his work, etc., *as far as* because if both are of equal power, this is of greater mercy.

hymns.title: And God will raise you up on eagle's wings
I am weak, but thou are strong
O Holy god, open unto me

praise.title: Just a Closer Walk with Thee

echoes.text: Yahweh says to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool for your feet.”
echoes.note: Seeing 'Jesus standing on the right hand of God' draws on the enthronement oracle 'Sit thou at my right hand,' the supreme OT proof-text of exaltation — strikingly with Jesus standing rather than seated.

echoes.text: I saw in the night visions, and behold, there came with the clouds of the sky one like a son of man, and he came even to the ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.
echoes.note: 'The Son of Man standing at the right hand of God' fuses Daniel's vision of 'one like the Son of man' coming with the clouds with the right-hand enthronement.

echoes.text: Into your hand I commend my spirit. You redeem me, Yahweh, God of truth.
echoes.note: 'Lord Jesus, receive my spirit!' reworks the Psalmist's 'into thine hand I commit my spirit,' the prayer of the dying righteous now addressed to Jesus.

echoes.text: The hand of the witnesses shall be first on him to put him to death, and afterward the hand of all the people. So you shall remove the evil from your midst.
echoes.note: 'The witnesses placed their garments' and the stoning reflect the Deuteronomic execution law that 'the hands of the witnesses shall be first upon him to put him to death.'

echoes.text: He who blasphemes Yahweh’s name, he shall surely be put to death. All the congregation shall certainly stone him. The foreigner as well as the native-born, when he blasphemes the Name, shall be put to death.
echoes.note: Stoning Stephen after the charge of blasphemy against the temple and God reflects the law that 'he that blasphemeth the name of the LORD... all the congregation shall certainly stone him.'

echoes.text: As the appearance of the rainbow that is in the cloud in the day of rain, so was the appearance of the brightness all around. This was the appearance of the likeness of Yahweh’s glory. When I saw it, I fell on my face, and I heard a voice of one that spoke.
echoes.note: Stephen 'saw the glory of God' in opened heaven echoes Ezekiel's vision of 'the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD,' the prophetic theophany pattern.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

events.label: The stoning of Stephen
events.note: Saul stands holding the coats and consenting to the death — the church's first martyr, and the first time we meet the man who will carry the gospel to the empire.

places.name: Mesopotamia
places.id: The land between the Tigris and Euphrates. In the apostolic period split between Roman client kingdoms in the upper basin (Edessa) and Parthian control of Babylonia. Pin sits in the middle Euphrates region.

places.name: Haran
places.id: Modern Harran in southeastern Turkey on the Balikh river, a major caravan and cult centre of the moon-god Sin from the third millennium B.C. Terah's family settled here from Ur (Gen 11:31); Abraham left from Haran for Canaan (Gen 12:4). Site of the Roman defeat at Carrhae in 53 B.C.

places.name: Egypt
places.id: The Nile valley civilization, the land of Israel's bondage. Pin sits on the Nile near ancient Memphis.

places.name: Canaan
places.id: The pre-Israelite name for the southern Levant, broadly the Mediterranean coastal strip and the highlands east to the Jordan. The term, attested in Egyptian and Akkadian sources from the second millennium, gives way to 'Israel' / 'Judah' through the biblical period.

places.name: Shechem
places.id: Tell Balata at the eastern edge of modern Nablus, in the saddle between Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim. The patriarchal sanctuary of Gen 12:6, 33:18-20 and the covenant-renewal site of Joshua 24. Excavations by Sellin and Wright revealed Middle and Late Bronze fortifications and a fortress-temple.

places.name: Midian
places.id: The Arabian region southeast of the Gulf of Aqaba, traditionally located on the eastern side of the Red Sea (modern northwestern Saudi Arabia). Refuge of Moses after his flight from Egypt (Exod 2:15); home of Jethro and the burning bush (Exod 3).

places.name: Mount Sinai
places.id: Traditionally identified with Jebel Musa in the southern Sinai peninsula, where the Monastery of Saint Catherine has been continuously occupied since the sixth century. Other proposals locate Sinai at Jebel al-Lawz in northwestern Saudi Arabia (matching a Midianite location for the burning bush), at Har Karkom in the Negev, or at Jebel Sin Bishar. The traditional Jebel Musa identification is preserved here as the long-standing default; the alternatives are footnoted.

places.name: Red Sea
places.id: The Hebrew Yam Suph ('Sea of Reeds') traditionally rendered Red Sea. The crossing-point of the exodus is variously located in the marshes north of the Gulf of Suez, in one of the Bitter Lakes, or in the Gulf of Aqaba; the chapter does not specify.

places.name: Babylon
places.id: On the Euphrates c. 85 km south of Baghdad. Capital of the Neo-Babylonian empire (Nebuchadnezzar II). Stephen's quotation in v. 43 modifies Amos 5:27 ('beyond Damascus') to 'beyond Babylon', reading the exile of 587 B.C. as the prophet's longer-range fulfilment.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: Oh taste and see that Yahweh is good. Blessed is the man who takes refuge in him.
echoes.note: "if indeed you have tasted that the Lord is gracious" (2:3) closely reworks Psalm 34:8 LXX (33:9), "taste and see that the Lord is good (chrēstos)." The verb 'tasted' plus the divine predicate is a strong verbal borrowing; the wordplay chrēstos/Christos prepares the turn to the living stone. Psalm 34 recurs across 1 Peter (cf. 3:10-12 quoting Ps 34:12-16), raising recurrence and volume.

echoes.text: The voice of one saying, “Cry!” One said, “What shall I cry?” “All flesh is like grass, and all its glory is like the flower of the field. The grass withers, the flower fades, because Yahweh’s breath blows on it. Surely the people are like grass. The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God stands forever.”
echoes.note: "long for the pure milk of the Word" (2:2) picks up the 'word' (logos/rhēma) by which the readers were reborn (1:23-25, where Isa 40:6-8 is just quoted); the abiding word of God is the nourishment metaphor here, an echo carried over from the immediately preceding citation.

echoes.text: Therefore thus says the Lord Yahweh, “Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious cornerstone of a sure foundation. He who believes shall not act hastily.
echoes.note: "Behold, I lay in Zion a chief cornerstone, chosen, and precious: He who believes in him will not be disappointed" (2:6) is a formula-introduced citation ("it is contained in Scripture") of Isaiah 28:16 LXX. Verbatim: tithēmi en Siōn lithon... eklekton entimon, and the believer not being put to shame. The keywords 'chosen/precious' also reach back to v.4-5 ('chosen by God, precious').

echoes.text: The stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner.
echoes.note: "The stone which the builders rejected, has become the chief cornerstone" (2:7) is a verbatim quotation of Psalm 118:22 LXX (117:22). Part of the stacked stone-testimonia catena; the same text is a primary early-Christian Christological proof (cf. Mark 12:10; Acts 4:11). 'Rejected'/'builders' ties to the rejection theme of v.4.

echoes.text: He will be a sanctuary, but for both houses of Israel, he will be a trap and a snare for the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
echoes.note: "a stone of stumbling, and a rock of offense" (2:8) quotes Isaiah 8:14, lithos proskommatos kai petra skandalou. Third member of the stone catena, applied to the disobedient who stumble at the word; combined here (as in Rom 9:33) with Isa 28:16.

echoes.text: and you shall be to me a kingdom of priests, and a holy nation.’ These are the words which you shall speak to the children of Israel.”
echoes.note: "a royal priesthood... a holy nation" (2:9) draws directly on Exodus 19:6 LXX, basileion hierateuma kai ethnos hagion, the Sinai vocation of Israel now applied to the church. High volume; the priesthood theme also undergirds v.5 ('holy priesthood... spiritual sacrifices').

echoes.text: The animals of the field shall honor me, the jackals and the ostriches; because I give water in the wilderness and rivers in the desert, to give drink to my people, my chosen, the people which I formed for myself, that they might declare my praise.
echoes.note: "a chosen race... a people for God's own possession, that you may proclaim the excellence of him" (2:9) is woven from Isaiah 43:20-21 LXX, 'my chosen race (genos eklekton)... my people whom I preserved to declare my excellencies (aretas).' The distinctive phrase 'proclaim the excellencies/aretas' is verbatim from Isa 43:21 and not from Exod 19, marking this as a separate source fused into the title-collage.

echoes.text: Now therefore, if you will indeed obey my voice, and keep my covenant, then you shall be my own possession from among all peoples; for all the earth is mine;
echoes.note: "a people for God's own possession" (2:9) renders laos eis peripoiēsin, echoing the 'peculiar treasure/possession' (laos periousios / segullah) of Exodus 19:5; reinforces the Sinai covenant frame alongside Exod 19:6, and resonant with Mal 3:17 / Isa 43:21.

echoes.text: I will sow her to me in the earth; and I will have mercy on her who had not obtained mercy; and I will tell those who were not my people, ‘You are my people;’ and they will say, ‘My God!’”
echoes.note: "who in time past were no people, but now are God's people, who had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy" (2:10) reworks Hosea 2:23 (LXX 2:25), 'I will say to Not-my-people, You are my people' and 'I will have mercy on Not-pitied.' The double not-people/people and not-mercy/mercy antithesis is the signature of Hosea, also taken up in Rom 9:25.

echoes.text: He said, “Call his name Lo-Ammi; for you are not my people, and I will not be yours. Yet the number of the children of Israel will be as the sand of the sea, which can’t be measured nor numbered; and it will come to pass that, in the place where it was said to them, ‘You are not my people,’ they will be called ‘sons of the living God.’
echoes.note: "were no people, but now are God's people" (2:10) also draws on Hosea 1:9-10, the naming of Lo-ammi ('not my people') and the reversal 'you are sons of the living God.' Companion source to Hos 2:23 supplying the 'not a people' title; high recurrence within the Hosea reversal oracle.

echoes.text: Therefore thus says the Lord Yahweh, “Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious cornerstone of a sure foundation. He who believes shall not act hastily.
echoes.note: "chosen by God, precious" (2:4) pre-echoes Isaiah 28:16's eklekton entimon ('chosen and precious'), the very words cited in v.6; Peter introduces the catena's keywords narratively before quoting, a deliberate framing device.

echoes.text: Therefore thus says the Lord Yahweh, “Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious cornerstone of a sure foundation. He who believes shall not act hastily.
echoes.note: "as living stones, are built up as a spiritual house, to be a holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices" (2:5) is a typological reading of the Zion-stone oracle: believers become the new temple founded on Christ the cornerstone, a priesthood offering spiritual (not Levitical) sacrifices. The figural new-temple/new-Israel construal organizes the whole pericope.

echoes.text: He will be a sanctuary, but for both houses of Israel, he will be a trap and a snare for the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
echoes.note: "coming to him, a living stone, rejected indeed by men, but chosen by God" (2:4) anticipates and conditions the catena: the 'rejected by men / chosen by God' contrast frames the stone testimonia of vv.6-8 and the figural identification of Christ as the temple cornerstone before any is formally cited.

echoes.text: The stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner.
echoes.note: "rejected indeed by men" (2:4) anticipates 'the stone which the builders rejected' of Ps 118:22 (v.7); apodedokimasmenon shares the rejection motif, weaving the psalm into the opening description of Christ as living stone.

echoes.text: The stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner.
echoes.note: "For you who believe therefore is the honor" (2:7) plays on Isa 28:16's 'precious/honor' (entimon/timē) as the antithesis to the builders' rejection of Ps 118:22, binding the two quotations into a single believe/disbelieve contrast.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: Surely goodness and loving kindness shall follow me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in Yahweh’s house forever.
echoes.note: Jesus' promise to receive disciples into the 'Father's house' where they will dwell forever figurally fulfills the psalmist's hope to 'dwell in the house of the LORD forever.' Coherence is strong: John repeatedly reads the temple/house of God Christologically (2:16-21), and the eternal abode (monai) recasts the psalm's permanent residence in God's house. Volume rests on the shared house-dwelling motif rather than a verbal quotation.

echoes.text: One thing I have asked of Yahweh, that I will seek after, that I may dwell in Yahweh’s house all the days of my life, to see Yahweh’s beauty, and to inquire in his temple.
echoes.note: 'One thing I have asked... to dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life' supplies the prototypical longing for permanent residence in God's house that 14:2-3 grants the disciples. Recurrence of the 'house of the LORD as abode' topos in the Psalter strengthens the case; the contestation is that John gives no verbal cue, only the dwelling theme.

echoes.text: How lovely are your dwellings, Yahweh of Armies! My soul longs, and even faints for the courts of Yahweh. My heart and my flesh cry out for the living God. Yes, the sparrow has found a home, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she may have her young, near your altars, Yahweh of Armies, my King, and my God. Blessed are those who dwell in your house. They are always praising you. Selah.
echoes.note: 'How lovely is your dwelling place... blessed are those who dwell in your house' frames the temple as the place of beatitude, the same register behind the 'many rooms' in the Father's house. Low confidence: thematically apt but adds no distinctive lexeme beyond the shared house/dwelling idea, and competes with the other Psalter echoes.

echoes.text: Let them make me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them. According to all that I show you, the pattern of the tabernacle, and the pattern of all of its furniture, even so you shall make it.
echoes.note: 'Let them make me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them' establishes the tabernacle as God's dwelling, the OT substrate John reworks when Jesus prepares an eternal dwelling-place and elsewhere reads his own body as the temple. Figural rather than verbal; the connection runs through John's larger temple Christology more than through 14:2 itself.

echoes.text: They set forward from the Mount of Yahweh three days’ journey. The ark of the covenant of Yahweh went before them three days’ journey, to seek out a resting place for them. The cloud of Yahweh was over them by day, when they set forward from the camp.
echoes.note: The ark going ahead 'to seek out a resting place' for Israel offers a faint Exodus-journey backdrop to Jesus going ahead to 'prepare a place' for his followers. Volume is weak and the lexical overlap thin; flagged low and contested as a possible wilderness-itinerary resonance rather than a deliberate citation.

echoes.text: Show me your ways, Yahweh. Teach me your paths. Guide me in your truth, and teach me, For you are the God of my salvation, I wait for you all day long.
echoes.note: 'Make me to know your ways, O LORD... lead me in your truth' fuses 'way' and 'truth' in a prayer for divine guidance, the very pairing Jesus claims to embody as 'the way and the truth.' Coherence is high with the Psalter's 'way of the LORD' theology; John transfers the divine path/truth that leads to God onto Jesus himself, who is now the access to the Father.

echoes.text: Teach me your way, Yahweh. I will walk in your truth. Make my heart undivided to fear your name.
echoes.note: 'Teach me your way, O LORD, that I may walk in your truth' again binds 'way' and 'truth' as the route to communion with God, paralleling 14:6's claim that the way and truth lead to the Father. Recurrence of this way/truth collocation across the Psalter raises Volume; the contestation is that John offers no formula-citation, only the absorbed idiom.

echoes.text: A highway will be there, a road, and it will be called The Holy Way. The unclean shall not pass over it, but it will be for those who walk in the Way. Wicked fools will not go there.
echoes.note: The 'Holy Way' on which the redeemed travel to Zion provides a prophetic 'way' that leads God's people home, figurally fulfilled when Jesus is the exclusive 'way' to the Father's house. Coherence with John's homecoming theme (14:2-3) is strong; the singular eschatological highway resonates with Jesus as the one road of return.

echoes.text: Behold, I have set before you this day life and prosperity, and death and evil. For I command you this day to love Yahweh your God, to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments, his statutes, and his ordinances, that you may live and multiply, and that Yahweh your God may bless you in the land where you go in to possess it. But if your heart turns away, and you will not hear, but are drawn away, and worship other gods, and serve them; I denounce to […]
echoes.note: Moses sets before Israel 'life' and 'the way' of obeying the LORD, the choice that is itself 'your life' and the means to dwell in the land. Jesus' self-identification as 'the way... and the life' recasts this Deuteronomic life-through-the-way into a person; Coherence is reinforced by 14:15's love-and-keep-commandments idiom drawn from the same book.

echoes.text: Yahweh passed by before him, and proclaimed, “Yahweh! Yahweh, a merciful and gracious God, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness and truth,
echoes.note: The LORD proclaims himself 'abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness (emet/aletheia),' the covenant 'truth' that John's prologue already applied to the incarnate Word (1:14, 'full of grace and truth'). Jesus' claim to be 'the truth' thus draws on the Sinai self-revelation of God's faithfulness; medium confidence given the strong Johannine recurrence of 'truth' language.

echoes.text: “Now therefore, my sons, listen to me, for blessed are those who keep my ways. Hear instruction, and be wise. Don’t refuse it. Blessed is the man who hears me, watching daily at my gates, waiting at my door posts. For whoever finds me, finds life, and will obtain favor from Yahweh.
echoes.note: Wisdom declares 'whoever finds me finds life' and blesses those who keep her 'ways,' supplying a way/life nexus mediated by a personified divine figure. Jesus as 'the way... and the life' through whom one reaches the Father parallels the Wisdom-mediator pattern; low confidence because the verbal links are diffuse and the Wisdom backdrop is more securely felt in John 1.

echoes.text: I have chosen the way of truth. I have set your ordinances before me.
echoes.note: 'I have chosen the way of faithfulness (truth)' once more couples 'way' and 'truth' as the path of covenant fidelity. It adds Recurrence to the way/truth motif behind 14:6 but is too generic on its own; flagged low and contested as cumulative support rather than a discrete source.

echoes.text: He said, “Please show me your glory.” He said, “I will make all my goodness pass before you, and will proclaim Yahweh’s name before you. I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will show mercy on whom I will show mercy.” He said, “You cannot see my face, for man may not see me and live.” Yahweh also said, “Behold, there is a place by me, and you shall stand on the rock. It will happen, while my glory passes by, that I will put you in a cleft of […]
echoes.note: Philip's 'show us the Father' directly replays Moses' 'show me your glory,' to which God replies that no one can see his face and live. John inverts the denial: the one who has seen Jesus has seen the Father, fulfilling the Sinai longing to behold God. High Volume and Coherence given the explicit 'show us'/'show me' request and John's programmatic 'no one has ever seen God; the only Son has made him known' (1:18).

echoes.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend. He turned again into the camp, but his servant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, didn’t depart from the Tent.
echoes.note: The LORD spoke to Moses 'face to face, as a man speaks to his friend,' yet 33:20 forbids seeing God's face directly; this tension is exactly what 14:9 resolves by locating the Father's visible presence in Jesus. Coherence with the surrounding Exodus 33 theophany strengthens the medium rating beyond the headline 33:18-23 allusion.

echoes.text: Yahweh spoke to you out of the midst of the fire: you heard the voice of words, but you saw no form; you only heard a voice.
echoes.note: At Horeb Israel 'heard the sound of words but saw no form,' codifying that God is heard, not seen. Jesus' claim that his words are the Father's and that seeing him is seeing the Father answers this aniconic tradition. Low confidence: thematic counterpoint rather than verbal echo, supporting the 'unseen God' frame behind the pericope.

echoes.text: I will raise them up a prophet from among their brothers, like you. I will put my words in his mouth, and he shall speak to them all that I shall command him.
echoes.note: God promises a prophet 'in whose mouth I will put my words... he shall speak all that I command him,' the pattern Jesus claims in 14:10: 'the words I speak are not from myself; the Father does his works.' The prophet-like-Moses speech-formula gives modest Coherence with John's sent-one Christology; low because John does not cite the prophet text here.

echoes.text: With him, I will speak mouth to mouth, even plainly, and not in riddles; and he shall see Yahweh’s form. Why then were you not afraid to speak against my servant, against Moses?”
echoes.note: Moses uniquely beholds 'the form of the LORD' and speaks with him 'mouth to mouth,' a near-vision that 14:9 surpasses by granting the disciples the Father in the Son. Faint, contested support for the seeing-God motif; the lexical overlap is limited to the shared theophanic register.

echoes.text: but your eyes have seen all of Yahweh’s great work which he did.
echoes.note: Israel had 'seen all the great work of the LORD that he did,' framing God's redemptive deeds as 'works' the people witness; Jesus speaks of 'the works that I do' continuing in his followers. Low confidence: 'works of the LORD' is a broad Deuteronomic idiom rather than a targeted source, offering only thematic coloring to 14:12.

echoes.text: Israel served Yahweh all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders who outlived Joshua, and had known all the work of Yahweh, that he had worked for Israel.
echoes.note: Israel served the LORD all the days that the elders 'had known all the work of the LORD that he did for Israel,' another instance of redemptive deeds as 'works.' It reinforces the OT 'works of God' register behind Jesus' 'greater works,' but is too generic to credit as a specific allusion; flagged low and contested.

echoes.text: Yahweh, you will ordain peace for us, for you have also worked all our works for us.
echoes.note: 'You have indeed done all our works for us,' confessing that human works are wrought by God, resonates faintly with 14:12's promise that believers will do the works Jesus does because he goes to the Father. Low and contested: a thematic affinity about divinely-empowered works rather than a deliberate citation.

echoes.text: Yahweh is near to all those who call on him, to all who call on him in truth. He will fulfill the desire of those who fear him. He also will hear their cry, and will save them.
echoes.note: 'The LORD is near to all who call on him... he fulfills the desire of those who fear him' undergirds the answered-petition promise of 14:13-14 ('whatever you ask in my name'). The granting-of-requests motif is widespread in the Psalter; low confidence because no single verse is verbally anchored, though it situates Jesus in the role of the request-granting LORD.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Do not let your hearts be troubled.
We trust in God; we trust also in Christ.
In my Father's house are many rooms.
He goes to prepare a place for us.
How shall we find the way?
Christ is the way, the truth, and the life.
Christ is risen!
Christ is risen, alleluia!

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Come, you whose hearts are troubled, you who are weary of the road; there is a house ahead with room enough, and a place already prepared for you.
Christ is risen, alleluia!
You ask the way, and he does not hand you a map; he says, I am the way — walk with me.
Christ is risen, alleluia!
Stone by stone he is building us into a home, a people, a living temple where God will dwell.
Christ is risen, alleluia!
So into his hands we commit our spirits, and we are not afraid.
Christ is risen, alleluia!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: Do not let your hearts be troubled; trust in God.
Christ is risen, alleluia!
In the Father's house there is room, and a place prepared.
Christ is risen, alleluia!
I am the way, he says; walk with me.
Christ is risen, alleluia!
Into your hands we come. Come, let us worship.
Christ is risen, alleluia!
